title: How This Mom Makes $48K/Month With Claude
key_points: Sandy Lee made $48,000 in May with the breakdown: $10K full-time job, $5.5K AI SEO consulting (Upwork client), $23K sponsorships, $2K from self-built app, $1K YouTube AdSense, $6.2K from newly launched School community

Started AI consulting on Upwork with no prior AI/SEO knowledge by applying to positions she didn't understand, using ChatGPT to learn everything and create N8N workflows, landing a $3K monthly retainer that grew to $5.5K after learning Claude Code
Grew YouTube channel from 200 subscribers to 10K in less than a month by copying successful video formats while adding personal authentic stories
Previous content creation (2018-present) teaching Spanish to Korean speakers grew to 550K subscribers across 3 platforms but generated almost no revenue due to lack of monetization strategy
Old content creation process took 6-8 hours to edit a 2-minute video using Premiere and After Effects with no competitor research or analytics
Uses Ikigai framework with four questions: what do you love, what are you great at, what does the world need, what can you get paid for - previously only focused on first two, now focuses on all four
Video that drove growth from 2K to 10K subscribers was 'how I automate 90% of my social media content using Claude Code' - combined copying successful formats with personal story

Built and monetized a creator studio app using Vercel (frontend) and Supabase (backend) that finds outlier videos, generates personalized titles/hooks/thumbnails, includes teleprompter and screen share features
Sponsorship deals this month: $3,500 + $3,500 + $5,000 + $550 + $8,000 = $23K total from YouTube sponsorships

Hook structure taught in her app: pattern interrupt opening, mirror the viewer's situation, reveal opportunity if they stay until end, state consequence if they don't act, build authority credentials, then transition
Recommends copying format/structure but being authentic (yourself) rather than original - cites Mr. Beast as example of biggest creator who still copies formats
Previous failed ventures include Amazon FBA, dropshipping, and Etsy - spent thousands on courses that taught already-saturated markets

Difference with AI opportunity: other markets are oversaturated with creators teaching past success stories, while AI is new and 82% of people haven't used AI, with only a tiny percentage knowing Claude Code or Claude Homework
Launched School community with nothing inside, charged low ticket to filter for serious members, filled content after people joined and paid
Strategy: build audience first to understand their needs, then create products/services - opposite of traditional approach of building product then marketing it
Worked on less than 3 hours of sleep during learning/execution phase while maintaining full-time job as regional manager of 25 people and raising 3 kids
Claude Code specifically solved workflow problems in two days that were previously difficult with N8N
Advises against chasing AI trend updates (mentions Hermes agent, OpenAI Codex examples) as it leads to non-execution - recommends executing and learning from results instead
summary:
Sandy Lee shares her journey from zero AI knowledge to a $48K month in an interview with Sabrina. She breaks down her income: $10K from her full-time job as a regional manager overseeing 25 people, $5.5K from an AI SEO consulting client sourced through Upwork, $23K from YouTube sponsorships ($3,500 + $3,500 + $5,000 + $550 + $8,000), $2K from an app she built, $1K from YouTube AdSense, and $6.2K from a newly launched School community. Her background is in sales and marketing with 10+ years experience managing $50 million accounts, with a political science degree and UN internship.

She started on Upwork six months ago by applying to AI and automation positions she didn't understand, using ChatGPT to learn everything on the spot. She admits to hating N8N but had ChatGPT create workflows to appear knowledgeable. Her initial $3K monthly retainer client grew to $5.5K after she learned Claude Code, which she says fixed her workflow problems in two days. She notes consulting is good for fast cash and learning but isn't scalable or recurring income.

Sandy had previous content creation experience from 2018, growing to 550K subscribers across three platforms teaching Spanish to Korean speakers. However, she never monetized that channel effectively - editing took 6-8 hours for two-minute videos using Premiere and After Effects, with no competitor research or format strategy. She followed only two parts of the Ikigai framework (what she loved and was good at) without focusing on what the world needed or what she could get paid for.

Her YouTube growth strategy involved copying successful video formats while adding authentic personal stories. A video titled 'how I automate 90% of my social media content using Claude Code' drove growth from 2K to 10K subscribers. She built a creator studio app using Vercel for frontend and Supabase for backend that helps find outlier videos, generates personalized titles/hooks/thumbnails based on the user's Ikigai profile, and includes a teleprompter feature. The app teaches a specific hook structure: pattern interrupt, mirror the viewer, reveal opportunity, state consequences of inaction, build authority, then transition.

She launched her School community with no content inside, charging a low ticket price to filter for serious members, then backfilled content after people joined. She emphasizes building audience first to understand needs, then creating products - the opposite of traditional product-first approaches. She previously failed at Amazon FBA, dropshipping, and Etsy after spending thousands on courses teaching saturated markets.

Sandy cites statistics that 82% of people haven't used AI, and only a tiny percentage know Claude Code or Claude Homework, arguing the opportunity is unsaturated. She worked on less than 3 hours of sleep during her learning phase while maintaining her full-time job and raising three kids. She advises against chasing every AI trend update as it prevents execution, recommending instead to execute first and learn from results.
